tourism.detail: Australian passport holders can normally visit for up to 90 days without a visa, subject to the current entry-authorisation and arrival-declaration rules.
tourism.next: Live-check K-ETA treatment for the travel date, especially after 31 December 2026.
tourism.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

meetings.route: Visa-free B-1/B-2 short visit for attendance and business contact
meetings.detail: Meetings, negotiation and business contact can fit a short visit when no service is delivered and no profit-making work is performed in Korea.
meetings.next: Carry the invitation and move any consulting, training or contracted delivery into C-4.
meetings.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

conference.route: Visa-free short visit for delegate attendance
conference.detail: Passive conference attendance can use the short-visit lane; joining the program as a speaker or trainer needs separate classification.
conference.next: Ask the organiser to state attendee, moderator, panellist, speaker and workshop duties separately.
conference.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

unpaid-speaking.detail: Lecturers invited by a government or nonprofit body for seminars, lectures or advisory work in the public interest don't need a short-term employment (C-4) visa.
unpaid-speaking.next: Check the host is a government or nonprofit body.

paid-speaking.detail: Paid lectures, training and professional services under 90 days use C-4, including work performed for a Korean organisation when the traveller remains employed or paid in Australia.
paid-speaking.next: Allow the mission's published processing window and have the Korean host prepare its invitation, registration and contract documents.
paid-speaking.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

book-launch.route: Short-visit lane for rights meetings; C-3 confirmation for an unpaid reading or C-4 for a paid appearance
book-launch.detail: Publisher meetings can remain business contact. An author talk, workshop or fee follows the speaking rule, while a Korean publisher, importer or bookseller should handle local stock and retail receipts.
book-launch.next: Split rights, royalties, appearance payment, imported copies and sales before asking the host to classify the launch.
book-launch.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

ai-teaching.route: C-4 for short paid lecture or training; E-1, E-2 or another appropriate long-stay status for continuing teaching
ai-teaching.detail: C-4 expressly covers paid lectures and training. An ongoing university, language or institutional teaching role uses the relevant long-stay work status rather than repeated visitor trips.
ai-teaching.next: Have the Korean institution classify subject, audience, contract, hours and duration.
ai-teaching.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

remote-work.detail: The route is for qualifying overseas business owners or employees with prior experience, sufficient income and at least KRW100 million medical cover. The framework was expanded in 2026 to a maximum three-year stay and now varies the income threshold by age and Korean region; Korean local employment and profit-making activity remain outside it.
remote-work.next: Use the live 2026 table to confirm Luke's age-43 threshold for the intended region and keep Korean speaking or client work on its own route.
remote-work.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

entrepreneur.route: D-8 corporate investor, D-8-4 technology startup or D-8-4(S) Startup Korea Special Visa
entrepreneur.detail: A visitor can explore the market, but managing or working in the Korean venture requires the relevant investment or startup status. The route depends on investment structure, innovation evidence and any government recommendation or points pathway.
entrepreneur.next: Use Invest KOREA or a Korean startup-support body to test the company, investment and founder credentials before incorporation.
entrepreneur.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

trade.route: Short visit for negotiation, purchasing and exhibition attendance; C-4 or operating status for service delivery
trade.detail: Meetings and purchasing can stay in the visitor lane. Installation, training, consulting or other contracted service in Korea can trigger C-4 even when payment remains offshore; an ATA Carnet can cover qualifying temporary equipment and exhibition goods.
trade.next: Separate the commercial transaction from any person-days of technical or professional delivery.
trade.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

artist.route: C-4 for paid short performance or media work; E-6 or another appropriate status for longer entertainment activity
artist.detail: The Australian Korean mission expressly includes paid music, media, sport and contracted entertainment in C-4. An unpaid cultural appearance still needs C-3/visa-waiver confirmation.
artist.next: Have the promoter list rehearsals, performances, recording, merchandise, payment and all venues.
artist.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

mixed-mission.route: Short visit for attendance-only segments plus C-3/C-4 or long-stay status for active delivery
mixed-mission.detail: Korea looks at the actual activity, not only the trip label or where payment lands. A mixed speaking, teaching, trade and performance schedule may need C-4 even if tourism and meetings are also included.
mixed-mission.next: Give one lead Korean host a single dated schedule and have the mission classify the principal purpose.
mixed-mission.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

filming.route: Short-term employment visa (C-4-5) for short shoots, E-6 for longer
filming.detail: Paid crew and talent need a work visa; sources conflict on whether a short shoot can run on tourist entry, so confirm first.
filming.next: Ask the Embassy of the Republic of Korea, and KOFIC about location support.

research.route: C-3-1 short-term general visit (or K-ETA visa-free)
research.detail: Academic data collection, conferences and meetings fit a short-term visit of up to 90 days if unpaid beyond living costs. Paid work needs a C-4.

laws.rule: Working is illegal if it's not specified in your visa, whether paid or unpaid. Authorities have fined, detained and deported Australians for breaching their visa conditions. It's difficult to change your visa type once you're in South Korea. If you plan to work, arrange a work visa through a South Korean embassy or consulate before you travel. Disputes over expected working and living conditions for Australians teaching English are common. Some Australians planning to teach English have faced penalties after they or their employment agent provided false documents to Korean immigration authorities. laws.rule: Serious crimes, such as murder, could attract the death penalty. It's illegal to take photos of and around: military zones, assets or personnel official buildings It's illegal to buy counterfeit and pirated goods. South Korea has strict anti-corruption laws for public officials. Public officials and their spouses can't accept meals, gifts or other benefits above set limits. 'Public officials' include: public servants teachers journalists employees of government-owned or funded companies Get legal advice to make sure you don't breach these laws. If you're involved in a commercial or legal dispute, authorities can stop you from leaving until the dispute is resolved. Same-sex relationships and
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Before you travel: contact the South Korean Ministry of Food and Drug Safety or email [see source] to check whether your medication is a controlled or illegal substance in South Korea check with the Korea Customs Service for information on restricted or prohibited items that may not be brought into the country ask your doctor about alternative medicines. You may need to apply for a 'bring in' permit. When applying, provide the generic name of the medication, as the brand name in South Korea may be different in Australia. It may take authorities more than 2 weeks to process your application.
laws.heading: Medications

laws.rule: To drive, you'll need either: a valid local licence, or an International Driver's Permit (IDP) and a valid Australian driver's licence (digital driver's licences may not be accepted) Get your IDP before you leave Australia. You need a South Korean driver's licence to drive if you intend to stay in South Korea for 90 days or more. You will need a certified copy of your Australian licence to apply for a South Korean driver's licence. When issuing you with a South Korean driver's licence, the local
laws.heading: Driving permit

laws.rule: Drones over 2 kg must be registered through the Drone One-Stop service, even for hobby use. Approval is needed to fly in many zones (airport control zones, parts of central Seoul, the DMZ, nuclear sites) and at 150 m or higher. Aerial photography needs its own permission from the Ministry of National Defence in addition to airspace approval.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Korean Won (KRW). You can change Australian dollars for KRW at local banks and money changers. Credit cards are widely accepted in hotels, restaurants, shops and taxis, particularly in cities and larger towns. On arrival, declare all means of international payment, including KRW notes, cashier's checks, or foreign currency over $US10,000 or equivalent. ATMs are available in cities and larger towns, but these might not accept some foreign debit cards. Be aware of card skimming. See Safety.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Respect age and status: use polite speech, bow slightly when greeting, and give or receive things with both hands. When drinking with someone older, turn slightly away. At meals, wait for the eldest to start, don't stand chopsticks upright in rice, and don't lift rice or soup bowls. Tipping isn't required or expected.
